items.caption:
Ebbinghaus's forgetting curve: a day after learning something, only about a third was left. Each review resets the curve, and reviews spaced closer as the exam gets near make it stick.

Cramrade plans those reviews backwards from your exam date and quizzes you only from your own notes. Beta, for students 18+. Comment PLAN and I'll send you the link.
items.tiktok_title: Why you forget what you studied yesterday
items.youtube_title: Why you forget what you studied yesterday #Shorts

items.caption:
Rereading feels productive, but testing yourself is what holds up. In Roediger & Karpicke's 2006 study, students who practised recalling a text remembered more a week later than students who reread it.

Cramrade turns your own notes into quiz questions, and each one shows the line it came from. Beta, for students 18+. Comment PLAN and I'll send you the link.
items.tiktok_title: Rereading vs quizzing yourself: which wins?
items.youtube_title: Rereading vs quizzing yourself: which wins? #Shorts

items.caption:
Four habits for midterm week: quiz yourself instead of rereading, spread study over several days, mix topics in a session, and sleep the night before. Practice testing and spacing are the two techniques Dunlosky et al. (2013) rated most useful.

Cramrade spaces your reviews from your exam date, closer together as the day gets near. Beta, for students 18+. Comment PLAN and I'll send you the link.

items.youtube_title: 4 study habits with research behind them #Shorts

items.caption:
AI quiz tools can invent facts. In Cramrade, every question has to quote the exact lines of your notes it came from. The app checks the quote word for word, and if it isn't there, the question is dropped.

So you only study what's actually in your notes. Beta, for students 18+. Comment PLAN and I'll send you the link.
